| 12 September | [Style/Abbreviations](abbreviations.md) | The general guidelines were updated as follows:<br>When they are used, abbreviations and acronyms should always be explained. The name or title should be written out in full the first time it occurs in**the main body of**a document, followed by the abbreviation in parentheses. **Thereafter, the abbreviation may be used in footnotes, figures, tables and boxes. If an abbreviation or acronym first appears in a footnote, figure, table or box, it should be written out in full again the first time it is used in the main body of the document.**<br>Alternatively, if a document contains numerous abbreviations and acronyms, a list may be included after the table of contents or at the end of the document if there is no table of contents. **A list of abbreviations and acronyms applies to the main document and to any annexes or attachments to it.** |

| 19 October 2020 | [Style/Capitalization](capitalization.md) | The guidance on transliteration of proper names in Arabic was updated as follows:<br>The definite article al is capitalized when it is the first element in a name and lower-case when it is in the middle; for example, Al-Jazeera, Al-Qaida, Mohammed al-Ansari. **The same practice applies to el, where used.** |
| 13 October 2020 | [Style/Spelling](spelling.md) | The entry "comorbidity" was added to the spelling list |
| 21 September 2020 | [Footnotes](footnotes/index.md) | The guidance on Repeated references was updated to read:<br>A reference is given the first time that a source or item is mentioned in the text. In resolutions, a reference is given **once only**, the first time that an item is mentioned, **whether** in the preamble or in the operative part. Once a reference has been given, it is repeated only when necessary for the sake of clarity or to change a specific element in the reference, such as a section or paragraph number.<br>**A. Repeated footnote references**<br>In a change from past practice, numbered footnote indicators are no longer repeated in resolutions. When a reference must be repeated, a new footnote with the identical text should be inserted.<br>Repeated footnote indicators **may be used** in explanatory footnotes. |
| 21 September 2020 | [Footnotes](footnotes/index.md) | The last two sentences on the guidance on Excessive referencing were updated to read:<br>**II. General instructions on footnotes and text notes**<br>**C. Excessive referencing**<br>In resolutions, an item is referenced once only, the first time that it is mentioned, whether in the preamble or the operative part. When it is necessary to repeat a reference, a new footnote should be inserted. |

Other italicized terms (e.g., non-English words, species names, ship names) used within an italicized title or heading should be set in roman. |

| 17 April 2020 | [Footnotes](footnotes/index.md) | Change in guidance on text notes and footnotes:<br>**II. General instructions on footnotes and text notes**<br>Footnotes, text notes or references directly in the text. In masthead documents, sales publications and **reports issued as** supplements **to the Official Records**, references to **masthead documents, including summary records or verbatim records, supplements**, newspaper articles, public statements, interviews, personal communications and material on a website may be given in footnotes, text notes or directly in the text, as appropriate.<br>**III.United Nations sources<br>B. Reports issued as supplements to the Official Records<br>Elements in the reference**<br>In documents and publications, supplements may be cited by giving the document symbol in **either** a text note **or a footnote** after the descriptive title of the report. |

| 28 February 2020 | [Footnotes](footnotes/index.md) | Example added to Footnotes, chapter 4, section F |
| 28 February 2020 | [Style/Punctuation](punctuation.md) | The entry on commas was updated as follows:<br>**Commas in pairs**<br>When a non-restrictive relative clause comes in the middle of a sentence, it is marked off by a comma at each end. It is also important to use commas in pairs in other parenthetical constructions:<br>**Not** "In article 4, paragraph 6 (a) of the Convention..."<br>**But** "In article 4, paragraph 6 (a), of the Convention..." [Note too that, in English, brackets are used in pairs "(a)", even where a single closing bracket is used in another language "a)".]<br>**Not** "The court, while preserving its independence should perform..."<br>**But** " The court, while preserving its independence, should perform..."<br>**Not** "... submit to the Committee for its information, a report on..."<br>**But** "... submit to the Committee, for its information, a report on..."<br>**Not** "At its 42nd meeting on 18 January 1996, the Committee had decided..."<br>**But** "At its 42nd meeting, on 18 January 1996, the Committee had decided..." |
| 28 February 2020 | [Style/Abbreviations](abbreviations.md) | The entries for Inter-American Development Bank and Islamic Development Bank were updated to reflect current usage |
| 18 February 2020 | [Communications](communications.md) | The guidance on attachments was updated to read:<br>The order of attachments is as follows: annex, enclosure, attachment. The heading “Enclosure” should be used for material that is separate from but attached to an annex; the heading “Attachment” is used for material that is separate from but attached to an enclosure. The heading “Appendix” should generally be avoided.<br>Roman numerals are used for multiple annexes, enclosures and attachments |
| 5 February 2020 | [Country names and currencies](country-names.md) | The currency name should be written in full if it is used only once or twice in a document or if there is any possibility of ambiguity. If a currency that is not well known is used several times in a document, its name should appear in full at the first mention, followed by its symbol between parentheses |

| 17 January 2020 | [Style/Capitalization](capitalization.md) | The third paragraph was updated to read:<br>**Initial capitals are not used as a mark of respect; neither does the use of lower case imply a lack of respect**. Certain words are capitalized when used in a specialized or restricted sense, the purpose of the capital being to point to the specialized or restricted sense **(e.g. Aboriginal people in Australia, *but* the consequences of climate change on indigenous communities, black pupils are closing the gap in educational performance on their white classmates).** |
